A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLDP research. All 26 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.11, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original continuous-control experiments, SMPL humanoid evaluations, D4RL comparisons, and representation-learning ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and ablations. The externally sourced FB-CPR oracle is distinguished from the work's own results.

M1.justification: Equation 7 and Algorithm 1 replace the expected pairwise feature inner product with a squared Frobenius penalty between the feature second-moment matrix and identity. These are nonequivalent objectives for the central anti-collapse component, substantially changing the specified method. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a correction to its description.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four ExoRL/DMC domains, 45 SMPL humanoid tasks, six D4RL medium/medium-expert datasets, and four-room gridworld visualization scenario.

E2.justification: Benchmark comparator membership is retained. However, Appendix A.11 changes the stated orthogonality objective used in the explicitly labelled FB comparison, L_Bellman + L_Ortho. Table 10 retains its scores, so this establishes a revised comparator specification without establishing re-evaluation.

E3.justification: Sections 5, A.3, and A.5 retain the evaluation metrics, episode counts, dataset sizes, representation dimensions, architecture settings, and training budgets. No revised evaluation protocol or new experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix A.11 revises the component-loss ablation's definitions: the orthogonality term changes, and the prediction-loss sum includes steps 0 through H instead of 1 through H. Its result rows remain unchanged. The regularization, horizon, architecture, USFA, and visualization analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain four-seed experimental summaries, ten-seed D4RL comparisons, standard deviations, Mann–Whitney U tests, and Welch tests with Holm correction. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 5 corrects Pointmass averages: without SN, 515.02 to 581.63; without A, 547.62 to 658.29; without both, 583.78 to 650.67. These match the unchanged per-task entries and narrow the ablation gaps. RLDP remains highest at 671.11; other reported scores and empirical plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 replace the abstract-MDP definition, Lipschitz assumptions, and successor-measure error bound with a one-step policy-return bound and a new multi-step extension. The new derivations introduce second-moment conditioning, linear-readout and latent-Bellman assumptions, occupancy coverage terms, actor/planning errors, and horizon-tail bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of simple representation learning, collapse prevention, competitive zero-shot control, and robustness on low-coverage datasets. The theoretical replacement does not revise these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly explains orthogonality through well-conditioned linear readouts and dynamics prediction through Bellman-residual control, explicitly qualifying the control guarantee by coverage and actor assumptions. Appendix A.11 narrows 'largest returns' to 'largest returns on average,' consistent with the retained Table 10.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link below the abstract. Algorithm 1 now specifies pooling states across sampled trajectory segments and computing the empirical second-moment matrix for regularization. Existing architecture and training-setting disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The theoretical rewrite removes citations and bibliography entries for Agarwal et al. (2025), A Unified Framework for Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning Algorithms, and Gelada et al. (2019), DeepMDP. The broader related-work discussion and positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the theoretical discussion and Appendix A.1. Other edits include citation punctuation, cross-reference wording, and an additional contact email. The overall section structure and experimental narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adds action-input arrows for later prediction steps. Appendix displays are repositioned, including Table 5 beside its discussion and Figure 11 and Table 10 on separate float pages. The empirical figure images and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical transparency through an explicit regularizer computation and a control proof with clearly stated assumptions. Correcting Table 5 removes overstated ablation gaps, and the code pointer aids reproducibility. The supported overall gain is limited: empirical results are essentially retained, and the PDFs do not establish how the revised loss definitions relate to the experiments producing those results.
